content:
Apple is expected to unveil its first foldable iPhone tomorrow, with rumours suggesting the device may be named iPhone Ultra. Below are some last-minute rumours circulating ahead of the event, offering a preview of what we might see.

Starting Price

A new Bloomberg report published today indicates that Apple's initial target starting price for the iPhone Ultra was US$1,999. However, with rising component costs, the price recently discussed internally has been adjusted to start at US$2,199. The report notes that iPhone Ultra versions with larger storage capacities could push pricing up towards US$3,000.

Delayed Launch in China

Leaker Instant Digital posted on Weibo today claiming that the foldable iPhone's launch in the Chinese market is likely to be somewhat later than in other regions. The main reason is that the device only supports eSIM, and China lags behind other countries in eSIM adoption and related infrastructure.

The iPhone Air also saw a delayed launch in China compared to other markets due to regulatory issues surrounding its eSIM-only design.

More Evidence of Touch ID

Developer Pdfu posted on social media this week providing further evidence that the iPhone Ultra will use Touch ID instead of Face ID. Of course, this has long been widely reported as one of the new device's limitations — this is simply additional corroboration.

iPhone Ultra Screen Crease

Apple originally hoped to produce a foldable iPhone with a completely invisible crease, setting it apart from other foldable phones on the market. Today's Bloomberg report notes that what the company ultimately produced is a crease that is "far less visible than those on currently available foldable phones." To achieve this effect, Apple developed a "hinge system composed of advanced titanium and aluminium alloy, paired with specially engineered protective glass."

So even though it falls short of a completely crease-free display, Apple still plans to market this "as one of the key competitive advantages."

MagSafe

There have been conflicting rumours about whether the iPhone Ultra will support MagSafe. Mark Gurman earlier brought good news in an interview: "MagSafe is there — everything I've heard says this foldable phone will come with MagSafe."

Wrap-Up

Do you have any last-minute predictions or guesses about the iPhone Ultra? Do you think the new device will be called the iPhone Ultra or something else? Let us know in the comments.
